3	/// A VCS action the toolbar can perform.
4	enum VCSRemoteAction: String, Equatable, Sendable, CaseIterable {
5	  case fetch, push, pull, abortRebase
6	
7	  var label: String {
8	    switch self {
9	    case .fetch: return "Fetch"
10	    case .push: return "Push"
11	    case .pull: return "Pull"
12	    case .abortRebase: return "Abort rebase"
13	    }
14	  }
15	
16	  /// Whether the action contacts a remote — drives the timeout budget and whether the command needs
17	  /// the auth-forwarding environment (`StatusCommandRunner.runNetwork`).
18	  var touchesNetwork: Bool { self != .abortRebase }
19	}
20	
21	/// Why a remote read or action failed.
22	///
23	/// Deliberately NOT folded into `VCSError`: that enum is the backend-*read* taxonomy
24	/// (`lockContention`/`staleSnapshot`/`partialData`/…) and `WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)`
25	/// switches over it exhaustively to choose a sidebar badge. `.authRequired` has no sidebar badge and
26	/// no sensible answer there, so adding it would force a meaningless decision in a function that
27	/// currently has a principled one for every case. Same reasoning that put `CIResolution`/`PRResolution`
28	/// beside their resolver instead of in `VCSModels.swift`.
29	enum VCSRemoteFailure: Equatable, Sendable {
30	  /// `git`/`jj` not on PATH. Distinct from `VCSToolVersions`' floor check, which runs at launch —
31	  /// this is the same condition caught at the point of use.
32	  case toolMissing(String)
33	  case timedOut(VCSRemoteAction)
34	  /// Credentials were needed and none were available.
35	  case authRequired(String)
36	  /// The host's key isn't in `known_hosts`. `BatchMode=yes` turns what would be an interactive
37	  /// confirmation into this, so it needs its own copy — telling the user to configure a credential
38	  /// helper would be wrong advice.
39	  case hostKeyUnverified(String)
40	  case noRemote
41	  /// Push rejected (non-fast-forward). The engine NEVER force-pushes; the UI offers Pull.
42	  case rejected(String)
43	  /// git refused because tracked files would be overwritten.
44	  case dirtyWorkingTree(String)
45	  /// A failed or killed `git pull --rebase` left `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` behind. The repo needs
46	  /// `git rebase --abort`, so the UI must offer that instead of a retry that will fail identically.
47	  case rebaseInProgress
48	  /// A repo lock was held — git `index.lock`/`packed-refs.lock`, or jj's `git_import_export.lock`.
49	  ///
50	  /// The payload is the lock file itself when we could find it on disk, and that distinction decides
51	  /// what the UI offers. **`nil` ⇒ transient contention**, so Retry is genuine: another command held the
52	  /// lock briefly and by the next click it is likely gone. **Non-nil ⇒ a lock file is sitting there
53	  /// right now**, and retrying fails identically every time — the same reasoning that makes
54	  /// `rebaseInProgress` offer Abort instead of Retry.
55	  ///
56	  /// A leftover lock is what a SIGKILLed git leaves: the runner escalates to `killTree` two seconds
57	  /// after SIGTERM, and SIGKILL cannot be caught, so git's own cleanup never runs.
58	  ///
59	  /// Workroom does NOT delete it. Whether a lock is truly abandoned or held by a git running right now
60	  /// is not knowable from outside the process — `lsof` can't be trusted for it, and removing a live
61	  /// lock corrupts the index — so this reports and explains, and the removal stays the user's call.
62	  /// That is also what git's own message tells you to do.
63	  case locked(VCSLockFile?)
64	  case other(String)
65	}
66	
67	/// A lock file found blocking a VCS operation.
68	///
69	/// Located by parsing the path out of git's own error, which names it exactly, then stat-ing it — so the
70	/// file reported is the one git actually complained about rather than a guess at which lock it might be.
71	struct VCSLockFile: Equatable, Sendable {
72	  let path: String
73	  let modifiedAt: Date
74	
75	  var filename: String { (path as NSString).lastPathComponent }
76	}
77	
78	/// What a remote-state read decided. Mirrors `CIResolution`/`PRResolution`, `keepPrior` included: a
79	/// transient blip must not blank a good toolbar.
80	enum VCSRemoteResolution: Equatable, Sendable {
81	  case state(VCSRemoteState)
82	  /// Not a git/jj repo, or a repo with no refs at all (a fresh `git init`).
83	  case absent
84	  case keepPrior
85	  case failed(VCSRemoteFailure)
86	}
87	
88	/// What an action decided.
89	///
90	/// There is deliberately no `okWithConflicts`: jj records conflicts *inside* commits and `jj rebase`
91	/// exits 0 when it produces them, so the exit code cannot distinguish them — and the working-copy read
92	/// that could is not safe to make here (it would re-enter `JJSnapshotGate` for the same project root,
93	/// which that type documents as a deadlock). `RemoteStateModel` upgrades a `.ok` pull to "conflicted"
94	/// from the status refresh it already triggers, after the gate has released.
95	enum VCSRemoteActionResult: Equatable, Sendable {
96	  case ok(summary: String)
97	  case failed(VCSRemoteFailure)
98	}
99	
100	/// The seam for VCS operations that **write** — remote state reads plus fetch/push/pull.
101	///
102	/// Separate from `VCSProviding` on purpose. That protocol's doc calls it "the single seam the app
103	/// **reads** VCS data through", and four resolvers construct providers freely and call them with no
104	/// gate. Putting `fetch` there would mean nothing structurally prevented a read path from firing a
105	/// network mutation — the opposite of what `JJSnapshotGate` exists to guarantee. Keeping writes on
106	/// their own protocol also gives the injected `StatusCommandRunning` a home: `GitProvider` and
107	/// `RustJJProvider` are stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere to put one.
108	///
109	/// This is the growth surface for the rest of the VCS write phase (commit/amend, bookmark management,
110	/// the deep jj ops), which is why it's a protocol with a factory rather than one standalone resolver —
111	/// otherwise each later operation re-derives repo kind and wires its own runner.
112	protocol VCSWriting: Sendable {
113	  /// Everything the toolbar renders, as ONE coherent snapshot.
114	  func remoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
115	  func fetch(path: String, projectRoot: String, remote: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
116	  /// `anonymousRevision` is used only by jj, and only when `@` carries no bookmark: it is the revision
117	  /// the auto-created `push-<change-id>` bookmark will point at. Compute it with
118	  /// `CLIVCSWriter.jjPushRevision(hasChanges:hasDescription:)` — pushing a bare `@` fails when the
119	  /// working copy is empty and undescribed, which is the state a fresh workroom sits in. Ignored by git.
120	  func push(
121	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String, setUpstream: Bool,
122	    anonymousRevision: String
123	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
124	  func pullRebase(
125	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String,
126	    tracking: VCSTracking?
127	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
128	  /// Recover a workroom left mid-rebase. git only; a no-op for jj, whose rebase is atomic and
129	  /// `jj undo`-able.
130	  func abortRebase(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
131	}
132	
133	extension VCS {
134	  /// The writer for a repo, or a typed error for an unsupported path. Mirrors `provider(for:)`, and
135	  /// routes on the same `repoKind(at:)`.
136	  static func writer(
137	    for root: URL, runner: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner(),
138	    makeProvider: @escaping @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding = { try VCS.provider(for: $0) },
139	    gate: JJSnapshotGate = .shared
140	  ) throws -> VCSWriting {
141	    switch repoKind(at: root) {
142	    case .jjColocated, .jjNonColocated:
143	      return CLIVCSWriter(vcs: "jj", runner: runner, makeProvider: makeProvider, gate: gate)
144	    case .plainGit:
145	      return CLIVCSWriter(vcs: "git", runner: runner, makeProvider: makeProvider, gate: gate)
146	    case .unsupported(let reason):
147	      throw VCSError.unsupportedRepo(reason)
148	    }
149	  }
150	}

152	/// `VCSWriting` over the real `git` / `jj` CLIs.
153	///
154	/// **Why the CLI and not the libraries.** SwiftGitX 0.4.0's `fetch`/`push` pass `NULL` for the options
155	/// struct that would carry `git_remote_callbacks.credentials`, so they have no credential path at all —
156	/// HTTPS authentication is impossible through them — and it has no `pull`. Shelling the real binaries
157	/// means the user's own credential helpers, SSH agent and config just work, which is the same bet the
158	/// status layer already makes with `gh`. jj has no Swift API for these at all.
159	///
160	/// Pure `static` arg-builders, parsers and classifiers carry all the semantics, so they are unit-tested
161	/// without spawning anything — the pattern `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` established for exactly
162	/// this reason.
163	///
164	/// ```
165	///                 ┌──────────── every network op ────────────┐
166	///                 │ runNetwork: stdin=/dev/null, BatchMode,   │
167	///                 │ askpass off, SSH_AUTH_SOCK forwarded      │
168	///                 └────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
169	///                                      │
170	///                 ┌────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐
171	///                 │  JJSnapshotGate.run(projectRoot:)         │  git writes too
172	///                 │  NEVER re-enter for the same root         │
173	///                 └────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
174	///                                      │
175	///     git ─────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────── jj
176	///  fetch → PROJECT ROOT (FETCH_HEAD    │   fetch → PROJECT ROOT (a workspace
177	///          is per-worktree; the root   │           has no .git)
178	///          is one shared answer)       │   push  → PROJECT ROOT (bookmarks are
179	///  push  → workroom                    │           repo-global)
180	///  pull  → root (fetch) + workroom     │   pull  → root (fetch) + workroom (rebase)
181	///  abort → workroom                    │
182	/// ```
183	struct CLIVCSWriter: VCSWriting, Sendable {
184	  /// `"git"` or `"jj"` — resolved once by `VCS.writer(for:)` so no method re-derives it.
185	  let vcs: String
186	  let runner: StatusCommandRunning
187	  /// For `currentRef` only. The app already has a canonical answer including jj `.ancestor` and git
188	  /// `.detached`; re-deriving it from `%(HEAD)` would lose both.
189	  let makeProvider: @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
190	  /// Serializes writes per project root. Applied to **git** as well as jj: a project's workrooms are
191	  /// `git worktree add` worktrees sharing one `.git`, so a lock lost mid-`pull --rebase` can leave a
192	  /// workroom wedged in a rebase.
193	  let gate: JJSnapshotGate
194	
195	  var refTimeout: TimeInterval = 5
196	  var fetchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
197	  var pushTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
198	  /// Generous because SIGKILLing a rebase is the one genuinely unsafe timeout here — it can leave
199	  /// `rebase-merge` behind. `classify` probes for that and reports `.rebaseInProgress`.
200	  var pullTimeout: TimeInterval = 300
201	
202	  // MARK: - Placement
203	
204	  /// Where an operation must run.
205	  ///
206	  /// **fetch always runs at the project root, for both backends.** For jj because a secondary
207	  /// workspace has no `.git` (the rule `WorkroomStatusResolver.ghProbeDirectory` already encodes for
208	  /// `gh`). For git because `FETCH_HEAD` is **per-worktree** — fetching inside a workroom would leave
209	  /// the project and every sibling workroom reading "never fetched" while their remote refs were
210	  /// perfectly fresh. At the root it's one fact every workroom of the project agrees on.
211	  ///
212	  /// **jj push also runs at the root**, because bookmarks are repo-global. Everything else runs in the
213	  /// workroom: push/pull act on THIS worktree's HEAD, and jj's `rebase` must rewrite THIS workspace's
214	  /// `@`.
215	  static func opDirectory(_ action: VCSRemoteAction, path: String, vcs: String, projectRoot: String)
216	    -> String
217	  {
218	    switch action {
219	    case .fetch: return projectRoot
220	    case .push: return vcs == "jj" ? projectRoot : path
221	    case .pull, .abortRebase: return path
222	    }
223	  }
224	
225	  /// The **common** git directory for a path — the one shared by every worktree of the repo.
226	  ///
227	  /// `.git` is a directory in a normal repo and a FILE in a worktree, containing
228	  /// `gitdir: <repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>`. That per-worktree directory has its own `FETCH_HEAD`,
229	  /// `HEAD` and `index`, so reading `FETCH_HEAD` from it after fetching at the root finds nothing —
230	  /// the root's fetch wrote the root's copy. Stripping the `/worktrees/<name>` suffix gets the shared
231	  /// directory, which is where a root fetch's `FETCH_HEAD` actually lands.
232	  ///
233	  /// Pure string work, no subprocess: `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is authoritative but costs a
234	  /// process for something two file reads answer.
235	  static func commonGitDir(at path: String) -> URL? {
236	    let dotGit = URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(".git")
237	    var isDir: ObjCBool = false
238	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dotGit.path, isDirectory: &isDir) else {
239	      return nil
240	    }
241	    if isDir.boolValue { return dotGit }
242	    // A worktree's `.git` file: `gitdir: /abs/or/relative/path`.
243	    guard let contents = try? String(contentsOf: dotGit, encoding: .utf8) else { return nil }
244	    let line = contents.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? ""
245	    guard line.hasPrefix("gitdir:") else { return nil }
246	    let raw = String(line.dropFirst("gitdir:".count)).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
247	    guard !raw.isEmpty else { return nil }
248	    let gitDir =
249	      raw.hasPrefix("/")
250	      ? URL(fileURLWithPath: raw)
251	      : URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(raw).standardized
252	    // `<common>/worktrees/<name>` → `<common>`.
253	    let parts = gitDir.standardized.pathComponents
254	    guard let index = parts.lastIndex(of: "worktrees"), index > 0 else { return gitDir }
255	    return URL(fileURLWithPath: "/" + parts[1..<index].joined(separator: "/"))
256	  }
257	
258	  /// `FETCH_HEAD`'s modification time. git rewrites it on **every** fetch, no-ops included (verified),
259	  /// so its mtime is a complete record of git fetches — including one the user ran in a terminal.
260	  static func gitLastFetch(commonGitDir: URL?) -> VCSLastFetch {
261	    guard let dir = commonGitDir else { return .unknown }
262	    let head = dir.appendingPathComponent("FETCH_HEAD")
263	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: head.path) else { return .never }
264	    guard
265	      let attrs = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: head.path),
266	      let date = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
267	    else { return .unknown }
268	    return .at(date)
269	  }
270	
271	  // MARK: - git argument builders
272	
273	  /// Every remote ref plus, implicitly, the remote names. No `--count` cap: with branch switching cut
274	  /// there is no picker to fill, so this only ever answers "which remotes exist" and "does my branch
275	  /// have a counterpart".
276	  static func gitRemoteRefsArgs() -> [String] {
277	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + [
278	      "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname)%00%(objectname)%00%(symref)", "refs/remotes",
279	    ]
280	  }
281	
282	  /// Exact two-way divergence, independent of the user's `push.default`.
283	  ///
284	  /// **Deliberately not `%(push:track)`/`%(upstream:track)`.** Under `push.default=simple` — git's
285	  /// built-in default — `%(push)` resolves to nothing for a branch with no upstream, and every
286	  /// workroom is `git worktree add -b`, i.e. has no upstream. Deriving counts from that field leaves
287	  /// the badge permanently blank on any machine not set to `push.default=current` (verified on git
288	  /// 2.55). It also sidesteps a branch whose `%(upstream)` is a *local* branch, which would otherwise
289	  /// produce counts against a ref that isn't on any remote.
290	  ///
291	  /// `A...B` with `--left-right --count` prints `<only in A>\t<only in B>`, so with `A = HEAD` the
292	  /// left number is ahead and the right is behind.
293	  static func gitCountsArgs(remote: String, branch: String) -> [String] {
294	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + [
295	      "rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", "HEAD...refs/remotes/\(remote)/\(branch)",
296	    ]
297	  }
298	
299	  /// No `--prune`: omitting it lets the repo's own `fetch.prune` decide, the same
300	  /// pass-NULL-and-honour-config philosophy `GitCommitDiff` documents. No `--no-write-fetch-head`
301	  /// either — `FETCH_HEAD` is exactly what `gitLastFetch` reads.
302	  static func gitFetchArgs(remote: String) -> [String] {
303	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + ["fetch", remote]
304	  }
305	
306	  /// `--set-upstream` only when there is no counterpart yet; passing it on every push would rewrite
307	  /// `branch.<name>.remote`/`.merge` each time. **Never** `--force`/`--force-with-lease`: a rejection
308	  /// becomes `.rejected` and the UI offers Pull.
309	  static func gitPushArgs(branch: String, remote: String, setUpstream: Bool) -> [String] {
310	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + ["push"]
311	      + (setUpstream ? ["--set-upstream"] : []) + [remote, branch]
312	  }
313	
314	  /// `--autostash` is mandatory, not a nicety: workroom trees are essentially always dirty, and
315	  /// without it every pull dies on "cannot pull with rebase: You have unstaged changes". The remote
316	  /// branch is explicit so a workroom with no configured upstream can still pull.
317	  static func gitPullArgs(remote: String, branch: String) -> [String] {
318	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + ["pull", "--rebase", "--autostash", remote, branch]
319	  }
320	
321	  static func gitAbortRebaseArgs() -> [String] {
322	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + ["rebase", "--abort"]
323	  }
324	
325	  // MARK: - jj argument builders
326	
327	  /// Read-only jj flags. `--ignore-working-copy` is REQUIRED on reads: without it every toolbar poll
328	  /// would snapshot `@` and take the working-copy lock (the house rule on `VCSProviding`).
329	  static let jjReadFlags = ["--ignore-working-copy", "--color", "never", "--no-pager"]
330	  /// Mutating jj commands must NOT carry `--ignore-working-copy` — the snapshot is what preserves
331	  /// uncommitted edits into the old `@` before the working copy is rewritten.
332	  static let jjWriteFlags = ["--color", "never", "--no-pager"]
333	
334	  /// One record per `(name, remote)` pair.
335	  ///
336	  /// Three verified traps in this template. The keyword is **`self`**, not `ref` (`ref.name()` errors).
337	  /// The `self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present()` guards are load-bearing —
338	  /// calling `tracking_*_count()` on a local ref renders the literal string
339	  /// `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>` into the output. And a colocated repo has a pseudo-remote
340	  /// called `git` that `--all-remotes` includes, which `parseJJBookmarks` drops.
341	  static func jjBookmarkListArgs() -> [String] {
342	    let template = """
343	      self.name() \
344	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.remote(), self.remote(), "") \
345	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.present() && !self.conflict(), self.normal_target().commit_id(), "") \
346	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.present(), "1", "0") \
347	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.conflict(), "1", "0") \
348	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.tracked(), "1", "0") \
349	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present(), \
350	      self.tracking_ahead_count().lower(), "") \

412	  struct RemoteRefs: Equatable, Sendable {
413	    /// Remote names, first-seen order (so `origin` keeps its natural primacy when present).
414	    let remotes: [String]
415	    /// Short names, e.g. `"origin/main"`.
416	    let shortNames: Set<String>

419	  /// Parse `for-each-ref refs/remotes` output.
420	  ///
421	  /// Skips records with a non-empty `%(symref)` — that's `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD`, whose short
422	  /// name is the bare remote and which would otherwise look like a branch called `origin`.
423	  /// Field count is checked rather than assumed: a ref name can't contain a control character, but
424	  /// being strict here means a malformed line is dropped rather than crashing the read.
425	  static func parseGitRemoteRefs(_ stdout: String) -> RemoteRefs {
426	    var remotes: [String] = []
427	    var shortNames: Set<String> = []
428	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
429	      let fields = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
430	      guard fields.count == 3 else { continue }
431	      guard fields[2].isEmpty else { continue }  // symref → origin/HEAD
432	      let refname = fields[0]
433	      let prefix = "refs/remotes/"
434	      guard refname.hasPrefix(prefix) else { continue }
435	      let short = String(refname.dropFirst(prefix.count))
436	      guard let slash = short.firstIndex(of: "/") else { continue }
437	      let remote = String(short[short.startIndex..<slash])
438	      guard !remote.isEmpty, slash < short.index(before: short.endIndex) else { continue }
439	      if !remotes.contains(remote) { remotes.append(remote) }
440	      shortNames.insert(short)
441	    }
442	    return RemoteRefs(remotes: remotes, shortNames: shortNames)
443	  }

445	  /// `"3\t1"` → (ahead: 3, behind: 1). `nil` for anything unexpected — never a misleading zero.
446	  static func parseCounts(_ stdout: String) -> (ahead: Int, behind: Int)? {
447	    let fields = stdout.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
448	      .split(whereSeparator: { $0 == "\t" || $0 == " " })
449	    guard fields.count == 2, let ahead = Int(fields[0]), let behind = Int(fields[1]) else {
450	      return nil
451	    }
452	    return (ahead, behind)
453	  }

455	  /// One bookmark, folded from its local row and its `@<remote>` row.
456	  struct JJBookmark: Equatable, Sendable {
457	    let name: String
458	    let tracking: VCSTracking?
459	  }
460	
461	  /// Parse `bookmark list --all-remotes` output into per-name tracking, plus the remote names.
462	  ///
463	  /// **jj's counts are inverted relative to git and are swapped here.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an
464	  /// `@origin` ref means *the remote is ahead of local*, which is git's **behind** — jj's own default
465	  /// template proves it by printing "ahead by N commits" next to `@origin`. One line, one comment, and
466	  /// a cross-backend integration test pins it.
467	  static func parseJJBookmarks(_ stdout: String) -> (bookmarks: [JJBookmark], remotes: [String]) {
468	    var remotes: [String] = []
469	    var trackingByName: [String: VCSTracking] = [:]
470	    var localNames: [String] = []
471	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
472	      let f = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
473	      guard f.count == 8 else { continue }
474	      let (name, remote) = (f[0], f[1])
475	      let present = f[3] == "1"
476	      let tracked = f[5] == "1"
477	      guard !name.isEmpty else { continue }
478	      if remote.isEmpty {
479	        if !localNames.contains(name) { localNames.append(name) }
480	        continue
481	      }
482	      // A colocated repo exposes a pseudo-remote called `git` (jj's local git-tracking bookmarks).
483	      // It is not a remote, and including it would both pollute the remote list and produce counts
484	      // against the local git refs rather than a server.
485	      guard remote != "git" else { continue }
486	      if !remotes.contains(remote) { remotes.append(remote) }
487	      // An untracked remote bookmark, or one deleted on the remote, cannot answer counts. `gone`
488	      // reports the deletion; nil counts report "unanswerable" rather than a misleading zero.
489	      let jjAhead = Int(f[6])
490	      let jjBehind = Int(f[7])
491	      trackingByName[name] = VCSTracking(
492	        comparedTo: "\(name)@\(remote)",
493	        ahead: tracked && present ? jjBehind : nil,  // swapped — see the doc comment
494	        behind: tracked && present ? jjAhead : nil,
495	        gone: !present)
496	    }
497	    let bookmarks = localNames.map { JJBookmark(name: $0, tracking: trackingByName[$0]) }
498	    return (bookmarks, remotes)
499	  }

501	  /// The newest operation whose description says it fetched.
502	  ///
503	  /// Matches a prefix rather than the whole string so a reworded suffix survives. The failure mode is
504	  /// graceful — one absent label, never a wrong one — and an integration test reddens on a jj bump.
505	  ///
506	  /// **Incomplete by design**: a `jj git fetch` that brings nothing prints "Nothing changed." and
507	  /// records NO operation (verified, jj 0.43), so this answers "last fetch that changed something".
508	  /// `RemoteStateModel` takes the max of this and Workroom's own recorded fetch time to close the gap.
509	  static func parseJJFetchOp(_ stdout: String) -> Date? {
510	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
511	      let f = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
512	      guard f.count == 2, f[1].hasPrefix("fetch from git remote") else { continue }
513	      guard let seconds = TimeInterval(f[0]) else { continue }
514	      return Date(timeIntervalSince1970: seconds)
515	    }
516	    return nil
517	  }

521	  /// Map a failed command to a typed failure. `nil` means success.
522	  ///
523	  /// `gitDir` lets a failed pull be upgraded to `.rebaseInProgress` — the distinction matters because
524	  /// that state must offer Abort, not Retry.
525	  static func classify(
526	    _ result: CommandResult, action: VCSRemoteAction, tool: String,
527	    gitDir: URL? = nil
528	  ) -> VCSRemoteFailure? {
529	    if result.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .toolMissing(tool) }
530	    let err = result.stderr + "\n" + result.stdout
531	    // A timed-out pull may have left a rebase behind; that reads better than "timed out".
532	    if result.timedOut {
533	      if action == .pull, rebaseInProgress(gitDir: gitDir) { return .rebaseInProgress }
534	      return .timedOut(action)
535	    }
536	    guard !result.ok else { return nil }
537	    if err.contains("Host key verification failed") || err.contains("REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION") {
538	      return .hostKeyUnverified(err)
539	    }
540	    if err.contains("terminal prompts disabled") || err.contains("could not read Username")
541	      || err.contains("could not read Password") || err.contains("Authentication failed")
542	      || err.contains("Permission denied (publickey)")
543	    {
544	      return .authRequired(err)
545	    }
546	    if err.contains("would be overwritten") { return .dirtyWorkingTree(err) }
547	    if err.contains("does not appear to be a git repository") || err.contains("No such remote")
548	      || err.contains("no such remote") || err.contains("No git remotes")
549	    {
550	      return .noRemote
551	    }
552	    if err.contains("Updates were rejected") || err.contains("! [rejected]") {
553	      return .rejected(err)
554	    }
555	    if err.contains("Failed to take lock for Git import/export")
556	      || (err.contains(".lock")
557	        && (err.contains("could not be obtained") || err.contains("File exists")
558	          || err.contains("Unable to create")))
559	    {
560	      return .locked(lockFile(in: err))
561	    }
562	    if action == .pull, rebaseInProgress(gitDir: gitDir) { return .rebaseInProgress }
563	    // A lock failure that never names a lock. git's message depends on WHICH internal step hit the lock:
564	    // a fast-forward pull reports `Unable to create '<path>': File exists.`, but a pull that must really
565	    // rebase fails in autostash first and says only `error: could not write index` / `fatal: Cannot
566	    // autostash` — no path, no "lock", nothing the checks above can match. That is the diverged pull,
567	    // i.e. exactly what the toolbar's Pull button is for, and it was landing in `.other` with raw stderr.
568	    //
569	    // So when the symptoms are lock-shaped, ask the DISK instead of the message. Deliberately last: any
570	    // failure git explains properly keeps its own classification, and this only speaks for the ones it
571	    // doesn't.
572	    if lockSymptom(err), let lock = existingLockFile(gitDir: gitDir) { return .locked(lock) }
573	    let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
574	    return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
575	  }

577	  /// Whether a rebase is parked in this worktree. Both directory names are checked: `rebase-merge` for
578	  /// an interactive/merge rebase, `rebase-apply` for the am-based one.
579	  static func rebaseInProgress(gitDir: URL?) -> Bool {
580	    guard let gitDir else { return false }
581	    let fm = FileManager.default
582	    return fm.fileExists(atPath: gitDir.appendingPathComponent("rebase-merge").path)
583	      || fm.fileExists(atPath: gitDir.appendingPathComponent("rebase-apply").path)
584	  }

586	  /// The lock file a failure is complaining about, or nil if we can't point at one.
587	  ///
588	  /// The path is taken from git's OWN message rather than guessed: git names the exact file it couldn't
589	  /// create (`fatal: Unable to create '<path>': File exists.`), and a repo has several lock files that
590	  /// mean different things — `index.lock`, `packed-refs.lock`, `HEAD.lock`, `config.lock`. Naming the
591	  /// wrong one would send someone to delete a file that isn't the problem.
592	  ///
593	  /// Returns nil for jj's import/export lock, whose message carries no path, and — deliberately — when
594	  /// the named file no longer exists: a lock that cleared between the failure and this check WAS
595	  /// transient contention, which is exactly the case where Retry is the right offer.
596	  static func lockFile(in stderr: String) -> VCSLockFile? {
597	    guard let path = parseLockPath(stderr) else { return nil }
598	    guard let attrs = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: path),
599	      let modified = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
600	    else { return nil }
601	    return VCSLockFile(path: path, modifiedAt: modified)
602	  }
603	
604	  /// Whether a failure LOOKS like it was caused by a lock, without saying so.
605	  ///
606	  /// Narrow on purpose. These are the symptoms git reports when it fails to take a lock through a path
607	  /// that doesn't print the lock's name; anything broader would start blaming a lock file that happens to
608	  /// exist for failures it had nothing to do with.
609	  static func lockSymptom(_ stderr: String) -> Bool {
610	    stderr.contains("could not write index") || stderr.contains("Cannot autostash")
611	      || stderr.contains("cannot lock ref") || stderr.contains("Unable to write")
612	  }
613	
614	  /// The lock files a repo can be blocked by, newest-relevant first. `index.lock` lives in the WORKTREE's
615	  /// own git dir; `packed-refs.lock` and `config.lock` live in the COMMON dir that every worktree shares.
616	  static let knownLockNames = ["index.lock", "packed-refs.lock", "HEAD.lock", "config.lock"]
617	
618	  /// The first lock file actually present in this repo, checking both the worktree's git dir and the
619	  /// common one — a workroom is a `git worktree`, so its `index.lock` and the repo's `packed-refs.lock`
620	  /// are in different directories.
621	  static func existingLockFile(gitDir: URL?) -> VCSLockFile? {
622	    guard let gitDir else { return nil }
623	    let fm = FileManager.default
624	    var dirs = [gitDir]
625	    // `<common>/worktrees/<name>` → `<common>`. Cheap and string-only; `commonGitDir` does the same trip
626	    // from a path rather than from an already-resolved git dir.
627	    if gitDir.deletingLastPathComponent().lastPathComponent == "worktrees" {
628	      dirs.append(gitDir.deletingLastPathComponent().deletingLastPathComponent())
629	    }
630	    for dir in dirs {
631	      for name in knownLockNames {
632	        let candidate = dir.appendingPathComponent(name)
633	        guard let attrs = try? fm.attributesOfItem(atPath: candidate.path),
634	          let modified = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
635	        else { continue }
636	        return VCSLockFile(path: candidate.path, modifiedAt: modified)
637	      }
638	    }
639	    return nil
640	  }

642	  /// The quoted path out of git's lock errors. Pure, so the parsing is testable without a repo.
643	  ///
644	  /// Covers both phrasings that quote a path — the bare `Unable to create '<path>'` and the ref-update
645	  /// form (`error: cannot lock ref 'refs/…': Unable to create '<path>.lock': File exists`), which nests
646	  /// two quoted strings and must yield the second.
647	  static func parseLockPath(_ stderr: String) -> String? {
648	    guard let marker = stderr.range(of: "Unable to create '") else { return nil }
649	    let rest = stderr[marker.upperBound...]
650	    guard let close = rest.firstIndex(of: "'") else { return nil }
651	    let path = String(rest[..<close])
652	    // Only ever report an absolute path to a `.lock`: a relative one would be meaningless to a user
653	    // reading it out of a tooltip, and a non-`.lock` match means the phrasing wasn't what we assumed.
654	    guard path.hasPrefix("/"), path.hasSuffix(".lock") else { return nil }
655	    return path
656	  }

658	  /// This worktree's OWN git directory — `<common>/worktrees/<name>` for a workroom, the same as the
659	  /// common dir for a project root. Rebase state (`rebase-merge`), `HEAD` and `index` live here, unlike
660	  /// `FETCH_HEAD` which `commonGitDir` deliberately resolves to the shared copy.
661	  static func worktreeGitDir(at path: String) -> URL? {
662	    let dotGit = URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(".git")
663	    var isDir: ObjCBool = false
664	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dotGit.path, isDirectory: &isDir) else {
665	      return nil
666	    }
667	    if isDir.boolValue { return dotGit }
668	    guard let contents = try? String(contentsOf: dotGit, encoding: .utf8) else { return nil }
669	    let line = contents.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? ""
670	    guard line.hasPrefix("gitdir:") else { return nil }
671	    let raw = String(line.dropFirst("gitdir:".count)).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
672	    guard !raw.isEmpty else { return nil }
673	    return raw.hasPrefix("/")
674	      ? URL(fileURLWithPath: raw)
675	      : URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(raw).standardized
676	  }

717	  private func gitRemoteState(path: String, current: VCSRef) async -> VCSRemoteResolution {
718	    let refs = await run(Self.gitRemoteRefsArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
719	    if let failure = Self.classify(refs, action: .fetch, tool: "git") {
720	      // A blip must not blank a good toolbar; a missing tool or a real error should show.
721	      if case .timedOut = failure { return .keepPrior }
722	      return .failed(failure)
723	    }
724	    let parsed = Self.parseGitRemoteRefs(refs.stdout)
725	    let primary = Self.primaryRemote(parsed.remotes)
726	    var tracking: VCSTracking?
727	    if let primary, let branch = current.name, current.kind == .branch {
728	      let counterpart = "\(primary)/\(branch)"
729	      if parsed.shortNames.contains(counterpart) {
730	        let counts = await run(
731	          Self.gitCountsArgs(remote: primary, branch: branch), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
732	        if let parsedCounts = Self.parseCounts(counts.stdout) {
733	          tracking = VCSTracking(
734	            comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: parsedCounts.ahead, behind: parsedCounts.behind,
735	            gone: false)
736	        } else {
737	          tracking = VCSTracking(comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: nil, behind: nil, gone: false)
738	        }
739	      } else {
740	        // No counterpart on the remote — the normal state of a fresh workroom, since
741	        // `git worktree add -b` sets no upstream. Reported as `gone` so the toolbar offers Publish.
742	        tracking = VCSTracking(comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: nil, behind: nil, gone: true)
743	      }
744	    }
745	    return .state(
746	      VCSRemoteState(
747	        current: current, tracking: tracking, remotes: parsed.remotes, primaryRemote: primary,
748	        lastFetch: Self.gitLastFetch(commonGitDir: Self.commonGitDir(at: path)),
749	        resolvedAt: Date()))
750	  }

752	  private func jjRemoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef) async
753	    -> VCSRemoteResolution
754	  {
755	    // Reads take no lock, so they stay ungated.
756	    let list = await run(Self.jjBookmarkListArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
757	    if let failure = Self.classify(list, action: .fetch, tool: "jj") {
758	      if case .timedOut = failure { return .keepPrior }
759	      return .failed(failure)
760	    }
761	    let parsed = Self.parseJJBookmarks(list.stdout)
762	    let primary = Self.primaryRemote(parsed.remotes)
763	    var tracking: VCSTracking?
764	    if let primary {
765	      switch current.kind {
766	      case .branch:
767	        tracking = current.name.flatMap { name in
768	          parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }?.tracking
769	        }
770	      case .ancestor:
771	        // `@` carries no bookmark — the normal workroom state, since `jj workspace add --name` creates
772	        // no bookmark. The bookmark row's counts would describe the ANCESTOR, not the user's work, so
773	        // count the actual revsets instead. `remote_bookmarks(remote=…)..@` is exactly what bare
774	        // `jj git push` sends, so the number and the button agree by construction.
775	        let ahead = await run(
776	          Self.jjRevsetCountArgs(Self.jjAheadRevset(remote: primary)), in: path, timeout: refTimeout
777	        )
778	        let behind = await run(
779	          Self.jjRevsetCountArgs(Self.jjBehindRevset(remote: primary)), in: path,
780	          timeout: refTimeout)
781	        tracking = VCSTracking(
782	          comparedTo: primary,
783	          ahead: ahead.ok ? Self.countLines(ahead.stdout) : nil,
784	          behind: behind.ok ? Self.countLines(behind.stdout) : nil,
785	          gone: false)
786	      case .detached, .none:
787	        tracking = nil
788	      }
789	    }
790	    // jj's fetch is invisible to `FETCH_HEAD` (it passes `--no-write-fetch-head`), so scan the op log.
791	    let ops = await run(Self.jjOpLogArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
792	    let lastFetch = ops.ok ? Self.parseJJFetchOp(ops.stdout) : nil
793	    return .state(
794	      VCSRemoteState(
795	        current: current, tracking: tracking, remotes: parsed.remotes, primaryRemote: primary,
796	        lastFetch: lastFetch.map { .at($0) } ?? (ops.ok ? .never : .unknown),
797	        resolvedAt: Date()))
798	  }

content.text:
Confirmed. The tooltip explicitly renders `rm "\(file.path)"` — a copy-pasteable shell command — with the lock file's path interpolated raw into a double-quoted string. `parseLockPath` only enforces `hasPrefix("/")` and `hasSuffix(".lock")`; a path may contain `"`, `` ` ``, `$`, `;`, etc.

Repository/lockfile paths derive from the workroom directory the user chose to open. If that directory (or a symlink target) contains a double quote — e.g. `/tmp/x";touch /tmp/pwn;".git/index.lock` — the resulting tooltip reads

```
rm "/tmp/x";touch /tmp/pwn;".git/index.lock"
```

Copy-pasting the tooltip advice (exactly the flow this feature is designed to encourage) runs the injected commands. `parseLockPath` stops at the first single-quote, so double quotes in the middle survive.

No other classic sinks were introduced: the Finder reveal uses `URL(fileURLWithPath:)`+`NSWorkspace.activateFileViewerSelecting`, which is not shell-interpreted; the disk probes (`attributesOfItem`) only stat; the `NSPasteboard.setString` copy is the raw path with no shell context.

return """
  A leftover lock file is blocking git.

  \(file.path)
  Created \(age).

  """
findings.explanation: `explain(_:now:)` interpolates the lock file path directly into a copy-pasteable `rm "..."` shell command inside the tooltip, and the whole design of the feature (`Copy Lock File Path` context-menu item, tooltip explicitly framed as `deleting the file is safe: rm "…"`) encourages the user to paste that command into a shell. `CLIVCSWriter.parseLockPath` accepts anything between `Unable to create '` and the next `'` as long as it starts with `/` and ends with `.lock` — a double quote, backtick, `$`, `;`, `\n`, etc. all survive. Lock-file paths derive from the workroom directory the user opened (`<repo>/.git/index.lock`, `<repo>/.git/refs/heads/<ref>.lock`, `<common>/packed-refs.lock`); ref-lock paths additionally embed the ref name, which git allows to contain many special characters. A user who opens (or is tricked into cloning into) a directory like `/tmp/x";touch /tmp/pwn;".repo`, or whose repo has a maliciously crafted ref name, will see a tooltip such as `rm "/tmp/x";touch /tmp/pwn;".repo/.git/index.lock"` and, following the app's own instructions, execute the injected commands. The Copy button copies the raw path, so if the user then types `rm <paste>` the same class of unquoted metacharacters injects at the shell.
findings.fix: Do not construct a shell command for the user. Either (a) drop the `rm "…"` line and rely on `Reveal in Finder` + a plain filesystem delete action, (b) render the path in the tooltip but wrap it in single quotes with all embedded single quotes escaped as `'\''` (POSIX safe quoting), or (c) tighten `parseLockPath` to reject any path containing shell metacharacters (`"`, `'`, `` ` ``, `$`, `\`, `;`, `&`, `|`, `\n`, `\r`, whitespace) and fall back to `.locked(nil)` in that case, so the shell-quoted advice is only ever emitted for paths that are safe to paste.
